candidates.explanation: Board clearly owns policy and orchestration through board-language ports and private adapters to narrow capability APIs. The dependency graph is acyclic, the RSC route uses the board surface, authorization is layered correctly, and unexpected failures have one designated reporting boundary.

The persistence-free board slice coherently owns orchestration and policy. Board ports and outbound bridges isolate narrow public capability surfaces; the route stays thin, capability authorization and board fail-closed policy are explicit, and the DAL owns unexpected-error reporting once.

The board slice owns the required policy, preserves an acyclic graph, exposes a board read entrypoint to the RSC route, and clearly defines layered authorization and single reporting. Dependency isolation is only partial against the rubric because it deliberately omits board-owned ports and adapters, directly composing published capability operations instead.

The board application query owns the cross-capability policy, uses narrow public capability APIs, preserves independence, and specifies fail-closed authorization with server-side reporting. It only partially satisfies the port/dependency criterion because there are no board-language ports or adapters, and the page imports the board application module directly rather than a distinct board RSC/public surface.
